slides.label: Fourth Proof: Holonomy To Gauss-Bonnet
slides.notes: This lecture presents holonomy as the fourth route to global Gauss-Bonnet. The proof begins with a loop measurement from parallel transport, temporarily extends the bookkeeping to open polygon edges, and then uses orientation cancellation and Poincare-Hopf to remove every auxiliary choice.

slides.label: Why Open Edges Need A Comparator
slides.notes: Closed holonomy compares a transported vector with itself after a full loop. An open edge has different endpoint tangent planes, so a comparator field is needed. The figure shows the warning numerically: two allowed fiducial fields give different open-edge deltas, while the comparison to the chosen field F produces the term that enters the proof.

slides.label: The Field F Supplies The Index
slides.notes: The nonsingular field F gives a reference direction on each edge, but it may have isolated singularities inside polygons. The index records how much F itself turns around a small loop. Subtracting two pi times that index prevents the edge ledger from charging curvature for the field's own winding.

slides.label: The Polygon Identity
slides.notes: The local identity is the engine of the proof. For each polygon, total curvature inside the polygon minus the index contribution equals the sum of Phi terms along its oriented boundary edges. This is a local accounting statement: curvature and index live in the region, while Phi lives on the boundary.

slides.label: Interior Edges Cancel
slides.notes: Now the local identity is summed over a partition. Every interior edge is traversed twice with opposite induced orientations. Since Phi of the reversed edge is the negative of Phi of the original edge, the two contributions cancel before any topological theorem is invoked.

slides.label: Closed Surface Mesh Ledger
slides.notes: The triangulated sphere and torus make the closed-surface hypothesis concrete. In a closed mesh every edge has exactly two incident faces, so there is no exterior boundary left over. The Euler characteristic is read from the partition by V minus E plus F, not by sampling curvature.

slides.label: Balance After Cancellation
slides.notes: Once all shared edge terms vanish, the equality reduces to total curvature equals two pi times the total index. The notebook check displays several genera: sphere, torus, genus two, and genus three. In each valid row the residual is zero, which is the computational shadow of the proof ledger.

slides.label: Proof Dependencies And Failure Modes
slides.notes: The dependency graph is useful because this proof is short but easy to misread. Open-edge comparison feeds Phi, the vector field feeds both Phi and the index term, orientation reversal feeds cancellation, and Poincare-Hopf is used only after the holonomy ledger has already become a total-index statement.

slides.label: The Fourth Proof In One Line
slides.notes: The final slide compresses the fourth proof into one line: local holonomy ledgers sum to total curvature, interior edges cancel on a closed surface, and Poincare-Hopf converts the remaining index sum into Euler characteristic. The result is the global Gauss-Bonnet theorem without a normal map or an embedding argument.
